source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ הַזִּפִים֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל הַגִּבְעָ֖תָה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲל֨וֹא דָוִ֤ד מִסְתַּתֵּר֙ בְּגִבְעַ֣ת הַחֲכִילָ֔ה עַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And came the Ziphites to Saul [at] Gibeah, saying, [Is] not David hiding himself on [the] hill of the Hachilah, on [the] face of the Jeshimon?

en.L: And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Is not David hiding himself on the hill of Hachilah, facing the Jeshimon?"
en.B: Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Did you know that David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the Jeshimon?"
en.R: Some men from Ziph came to Saul at Gibeah. They told him, "David is hiding on Hachilah Hill, across from the desert wasteland."

es.L: Y vinieron los zifeos a Saúl, a Guibeá, diciendo: «¿No está David escondido en la colina de Haquila, frente al Jesimón?».
es.B: Entonces los zifeos fueron a ver a Saúl en Guibeá y le dijeron: «¿Sabías que David está escondido en la colina de Haquila, que da frente al Jesimón?».
es.R: Unos hombres de Zif fueron a ver a Saúl en Guibeá. Le dijeron: «David está escondido en la colina de Haquila, frente al desierto».

fr.L: Et les Ziphiens vinrent auprès de Saül à Guibea, en disant : « David ne se cache-t-il pas sur la colline de Hakila, en face du Yeshimôn ? »
fr.B: Les Ziphiens vinrent trouver Saül à Guibea et lui dirent : « Sais-tu que David se cache sur la colline de Hakila, qui fait face au Yeshimôn ? »
fr.R: Des hommes de Ziph sont venus voir Saül à Guibea. Ils lui ont dit : « David se cache sur la colline de Hakila, en face du désert du Yeshimôn. »

vi.L: Người Xíp đến gặp Sau-lơ tại Ghi-bê-a và nói: "Chẳng phải Đa-vít đang ẩn náu trên đồi Ha-ki-la, đối diện Giê-si-môn sao?"
vi.B: Bấy giờ người Xíp đến gặp Sau-lơ tại Ghi-bê-a và tâu: "Bệ hạ có biết Đa-vít đang ẩn náu trên đồi Ha-ki-la, đối diện Giê-si-môn không?"
vi.R: Có mấy người ở Xíp đến gặp Sau-lơ tại Ghi-bê-a. Họ tâu với vua: "Đa-vít đang trốn trên đồi Ha-ki-la, đối diện vùng hoang địa."

decisions.choice: the Ziphites betray David a second time
decisions.reason: The people of Ziph had already told Saul where David was hiding, in almost the same words, and named the same hill of Hachilah (23:19). The story that follows runs closely parallel to chapter 24, where David also spared Saul's life.

decisions.choice: on the face of the Jeshimon: facing the wasteland
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "facing" or "overlooking", and it can also mean "east of", since the Hebrew way of giving directions faces east. The Jeshimon, "the desolate land", is the barren country that falls away toward the Dead Sea (23:19, 24).

decisions.choice: is not David hiding: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The question is a way of announcing news: the Ziphites are telling Saul where David is.

decisions.choice: Did you know that
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the "is not ...?" question into a natural English question that brings news; Readable makes it a plain statement.

decisions.choice: the desert wasteland
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name Jeshimon; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם שָׁא֗וּל וַיֵּ֨רֶד֙ אֶל־מִדְבַּר־זִ֔יף וְאִתּ֛וֹ שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת־אֲלָפִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ בְּחוּרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד בְּמִדְבַּר־זִֽיף׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Saul and went down to [the] wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand men, chosen [ones] of Israel, to seek David in [the] wilderness of Ziph.

en.L: And Saul rose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him [were] three thousand men, chosen [men] of Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
en.B: So Saul got up and went down into the wilderness of Ziph, taking three thousand of Israel's best soldiers, to hunt for David in the wilderness of Ziph.
en.R: So Saul took three thousand of the best soldiers in Israel and went down into the desert near Ziph to look for David.

es.L: Y se levantó Saúl y bajó al desierto de Zif, y con él tres mil hombres escogidos de Israel, para buscar a David en el desierto de Zif.
es.B: Así que Saúl se puso en marcha y bajó al desierto de Zif con tres mil de los mejores soldados de Israel, para buscar a David en el desierto de Zif.
es.R: Así que Saúl tomó a tres mil de los mejores soldados de Israel y bajó al desierto cerca de Zif para buscar a David.

fr.L: Et Saül se leva et descendit au désert de Ziph, et avec lui trois mille hommes, l’élite d’Israël, pour chercher David dans le désert de Ziph.
fr.B: Saül se mit donc en route et descendit dans le désert de Ziph avec trois mille des meilleurs soldats d’Israël, pour traquer David dans le désert de Ziph.
fr.R: Alors Saül a pris trois mille des meilleurs soldats d’Israël, et il est descendu dans le désert, près de Ziph, pour chercher David.

vi.L: Sau-lơ đứng dậy đi xuống hoang mạc Xíp, có ba ngàn người được chọn trong Y-sơ-ra-ên đi với ông, để tìm Đa-vít trong hoang mạc Xíp.
vi.B: Vậy Sau-lơ đứng dậy đi xuống hoang mạc Xíp, đem theo ba ngàn quân tinh nhuệ của Y-sơ-ra-ên, để lùng tìm Đa-vít trong hoang mạc Xíp.
vi.R: Vậy Sau-lơ đem theo ba ngàn người lính giỏi nhất của Y-sơ-ra-ên và đi xuống hoang mạc gần Xíp để tìm Đa-vít.

decisions.choice: three thousand chosen men: picked fighting men
decisions.reason: "Chosen" men are men picked for their skill as soldiers. Saul took the same number when he hunted David near En Gedi (24:3).

decisions.choice: went down: from the hill country to the dry land
decisions.reason: Gibeah lies in the central hills; the wilderness of Ziph is lower ground in the southern hills of Judah, falling away to the east.

decisions.choice: best soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "chosen men" were; Literal keeps "chosen".

decisions.choice: the desert near Ziph
decisions.reason: Readable uses "desert" for the wild, dry land the Hebrew calls a wilderness.

source.text: וַיִּ֨חַן שָׁא֜וּל בְּגִבְעַ֣ת הַחֲכִילָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹ֖ן עַל־הַדָּ֑רֶךְ וְדָוִד֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וַיַּ֕רְא כִּ֣י בָ֥א שָׁא֛וּל אַחֲרָ֖יו הַמִּדְבָּֽרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And camped Saul on [the] hill of the Hachilah, which [is] on [the] face of the Jeshimon, by the road; and David [was] staying in the wilderness, and he saw that had come Saul after him to the wilderness.

en.L: And Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which [is] facing the Jeshimon, beside the road, while David was staying in the wilderness. And he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
en.B: Saul made camp beside the road on the hill of Hachilah, facing the Jeshimon. David was living out in the wilderness, and he realized that Saul had followed him there.
en.R: Saul set up camp beside the road on Hachilah Hill, across from the desert wasteland. David was staying out in the desert, and he found out that Saul had come after him.

es.L: Y acampó Saúl en la colina de Haquila, que [está] frente al Jesimón, junto al camino, mientras David se quedaba en el desierto. Y vio que Saúl había venido tras él al desierto.
es.B: Saúl acampó junto al camino, en la colina de Haquila, frente al Jesimón. David vivía en el desierto, y se dio cuenta de que Saúl lo había seguido hasta allí.
es.R: Saúl puso su campamento junto al camino, en la colina de Haquila, frente al desierto. David estaba en el desierto, y se enteró de que Saúl había venido tras él.

fr.L: Et Saül campa sur la colline de Hakila, qui [est] en face du Yeshimôn, près du chemin, tandis que David demeurait dans le désert. Et il vit que Saül était venu après lui dans le désert.
fr.B: Saül installa son camp près du chemin, sur la colline de Hakila, face au Yeshimôn. David vivait dans le désert, et il se rendit compte que Saül l’y avait suivi.
fr.R: Saül a installé son camp au bord du chemin, sur la colline de Hakila, en face du désert du Yeshimôn. David restait dans le désert, et il a appris que Saül était venu le poursuivre.

vi.L: Sau-lơ đóng trại trên đồi Ha-ki-la, đối diện Giê-si-môn, bên cạnh đường, còn Đa-vít thì ở trong hoang mạc. Ông thấy Sau-lơ đã đến theo mình vào hoang mạc.
vi.B: Sau-lơ đóng trại bên đường trên đồi Ha-ki-la, đối diện Giê-si-môn. Đa-vít thì đang sống trong hoang mạc, và ông nhận ra Sau-lơ đã theo mình đến đó.
vi.R: Sau-lơ đóng trại bên đường trên đồi Ha-ki-la, đối diện vùng hoang địa. Đa-vít đang ở ngoài hoang mạc, và ông biết được Sau-lơ đã đuổi theo mình.

decisions.choice: David was staying in the wilderness: not on the hill itself
decisions.reason: Saul camps on the very hill the Ziphites had named, but David has moved on, deeper into the wilderness, where he can watch the camp.

decisions.choice: he saw: he became aware
decisions.reason: "See" here means to learn or realize. David hears of Saul's coming and then sends spies to make sure (verse 4).

decisions.choice: realized; found out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "saw" here; Literal keeps "saw".

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד מְרַגְּלִ֑ים וַיֵּ֕דַע כִּֽי־בָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל אֶל־נָכֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent David spies, and knew that had come Saul for certain.

en.L: And David sent out spies, and he knew that Saul had certainly come.
en.B: So David sent out scouts and learned that Saul had indeed arrived.
en.R: So David sent out spies, and he learned that Saul really had come.

es.L: Y envió David espías, y supo que Saúl ciertamente había venido.
es.B: Entonces David envió exploradores y supo que Saúl en verdad había llegado.
es.R: Así que David envió espías, y supo que Saúl de verdad había venido.

fr.L: Et David envoya des espions, et il sut que Saül était venu, c’était certain.
fr.B: David envoya donc des éclaireurs et apprit que Saül était bien arrivé.
fr.R: Alors David a envoyé des espions, et il a appris que Saül était vraiment venu.

vi.L: Đa-vít sai thám tử đi, và biết chắc chắn Sau-lơ đã đến.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít sai người đi dò thám và biết được Sau-lơ quả đã đến.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít sai người đi do thám, và ông biết được Sau-lơ thật sự đã đến.

decisions.choice: for certain: beyond doubt
decisions.reason: The two words mean "for sure" or "with certainty", as in 23:23. They could also be read as a place, "to Nacon", or as "to a fixed place", but no such place is known here.

decisions.choice: scouts
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "scouts" for men sent to watch an enemy's movements; Literal and Readable say "spies".

source.text: וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיָּבֹא֮ אֶֽל־הַמָּקוֹם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָנָה־שָׁ֣ם שָׁאוּל֒ וַיַּ֣רְא דָּוִ֗ד אֶת־הַמָּקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָֽׁכַב־שָׁ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וְאַבְנֵ֥ר בֶּן־נֵ֖ר שַׂר־צְבָא֑וֹ וְשָׁאוּל֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב בַּמַּעְגָּ֔ל וְהָעָ֖ם חֹנִ֥ים סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose David and came to the place where had camped there Saul, and saw David the place where lay there Saul and Abner son of Ner, commander of his army; and Saul [was] lying in the encampment, and the people [were] camping around him.

en.L: And David rose and came to the place where Saul had camped. And David saw the place where Saul lay, and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army; and Saul was lying inside the encampment, and the people were camping around him.
en.B: Then David set out and came to the place where Saul had made camp. He saw where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army, were lying. Saul lay inside the ring of the camp, with the troops camped all around him.
en.R: Then David went to the place where Saul's army had set up camp. He could see where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the army commander, were lying down. Saul was lying in the middle of the camp, and his soldiers were camped all around him.

es.L: Y se levantó David y llegó al lugar donde Saúl había acampado. Y vio David el lugar donde dormían Saúl y Abner hijo de Ner, jefe de su ejército; y Saúl dormía dentro del cerco del campamento, y el pueblo acampaba alrededor de él.
es.B: Entonces David se puso en marcha y llegó al lugar donde Saúl había acampado. Vio dónde estaban acostados Saúl y Abner hijo de Ner, el jefe de su ejército. Saúl dormía dentro del cerco del campamento, con las tropas acampadas a su alrededor.
es.R: Entonces David fue al lugar donde el ejército de Saúl había acampado. Pudo ver dónde estaban acostados Saúl y Abner hijo de Ner, el jefe del ejército. Saúl estaba acostado en medio del campamento, y sus soldados acampaban a su alrededor.

fr.L: Et David se leva et vint à l’endroit où Saül campait. Et David vit l’endroit où étaient couchés Saül et Abner, fils de Ner, le chef de son armée ; et Saül était couché à l’intérieur du campement, et le peuple campait autour de lui.
fr.B: Puis David se mit en route et arriva à l’endroit où Saül avait établi son camp. Il vit où étaient couchés Saül et Abner, fils de Ner, le chef de son armée. Saül était couché à l’intérieur du cercle du camp, et les troupes campaient tout autour de lui.
fr.R: Ensuite, David est allé à l’endroit où l’armée de Saül avait installé son camp. Il a vu où Saül et Abner, fils de Ner, le chef de l’armée, étaient couchés. Saül était couché au milieu du camp, et ses soldats campaient tout autour de lui.

vi.L: Đa-vít đứng dậy đi đến chỗ Sau-lơ đã đóng trại. Đa-vít thấy chỗ Sau-lơ nằm, cùng Áp-ne con trai Nê-rơ, tướng chỉ huy quân đội của ông; Sau-lơ nằm bên trong vòng trại, còn quân lính đóng trại chung quanh ông.
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít lên đường đến chỗ Sau-lơ đóng trại. Ông thấy chỗ Sau-lơ và Áp-ne con trai Nê-rơ, tướng chỉ huy quân đội, đang nằm. Sau-lơ nằm bên trong vòng trại, quân lính đóng trại chung quanh.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít đi đến chỗ quân của Sau-lơ đóng trại. Ông thấy chỗ Sau-lơ và Áp-ne con trai Nê-rơ, tướng chỉ huy quân đội, đang nằm. Sau-lơ nằm ở giữa trại, còn quân lính đóng trại chung quanh vua.

decisions.choice: Abner son of Ner, commander of his army
decisions.reason: Abner was Saul's cousin and the commander of his army (14:50-51). As the king's chief soldier he had the duty of guarding him, which David will throw back at him (verses 15-16).

decisions.choice: the encampment: the ring of the camp
decisions.reason: As in 17:20, the word names a circle or track, probably the inner ring of the camp, perhaps marked by carts or baggage. The king slept at the center, protected on every side.

decisions.choice: the people: the army
decisions.reason: "The people" here are Saul's fighting men camped in the field.

decisions.choice: the troops; his soldiers
decisions.reason: For the people as an army in the field, Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "soldiers"; Literal keeps "the people".

decisions.choice: the ring of the camp
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the circle; Readable says "the middle of the camp".

decisions.choice: le chef de l'armée
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for "commander of the army", at every level.

decisions.choice: "tướng chỉ huy quân đội"
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's form for the commander of the army; Abner's father is "Nê-rơ".

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן דָּוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀אֶל־אֲחִימֶ֣לֶךְ הַחִתִּ֗י וְאֶל־אֲבִישַׁ֨י בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֜ה אֲחִ֤י יוֹאָב֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מִֽי־יֵרֵ֥ד אִתִּ֛י אֶל־שָׁא֖וּל אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִישַׁ֔י אֲנִ֖י אֵרֵ֥ד עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, saying, Who will go down with me to Saul to the camp? And said Abishai, I will go down with you.

en.L: And David answered and said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, saying, "Who will go down with me to Saul, into the camp?" And Abishai said, "I will go down with you."
en.B: David turned to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and asked, "Who will go down with me into the camp, to Saul?" "I will go with you," Abishai answered.
en.R: David spoke to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai, Joab's brother, whose mother was Zeruiah. He asked them, "Who will go down with me into Saul's camp?" Abishai said, "I will go with you."

es.L: Y habló David y dijo a Ahimelec el hitita y a Abisai hijo de Sarvia, hermano de Joab: «¿Quién bajará conmigo a Saúl, al campamento?». Y dijo Abisai: «Yo bajaré contigo».
es.B: David se dirigió a Ahimelec el hitita y a Abisai hijo de Sarvia, hermano de Joab, y les preguntó: «¿Quién bajará conmigo al campamento, adonde está Saúl?». «Yo iré contigo», le respondió Abisai.
es.R: David habló con Ahimelec el hitita y con Abisai, el hermano de Joab, cuya madre era Sarvia. Les preguntó: «¿Quién bajará conmigo al campamento de Saúl?». Abisai le dijo: «Yo iré contigo».

fr.L: Et David prit la parole et dit à Ahimélek le Hittite et à Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, frère de Joab : « Qui descendra avec moi vers Saül, dans le camp ? » Et Abishaï dit : « Moi, je descendrai avec toi. »
fr.B: David s’adressa à Ahimélek le Hittite et à Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, frère de Joab : « Qui veut descendre avec moi dans le camp, jusqu’à Saül ? » « Moi, j’irai avec toi », répondit Abishaï.
fr.R: David a parlé à Ahimélek le Hittite et à Abishaï, le frère de Joab, dont la mère s’appelait Tserouya. Il leur a demandé : « Qui veut descendre avec moi dans le camp de Saül ? » Abishaï a répondu : « Moi, je vais avec toi. »

vi.L: Đa-vít lên tiếng nói với A-hi-mê-léc người Hê-tít và với A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia, anh em với Giô-áp: "Ai sẽ cùng tôi đi xuống trại quân, đến chỗ Sau-lơ?" A-bi-sai nói: "Tôi sẽ cùng ông đi xuống."
vi.B: Đa-vít quay sang hỏi A-hi-mê-léc người Hê-tít và A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia, anh em với Giô-áp: "Ai sẽ cùng tôi xuống trại quân, đến chỗ Sau-lơ?" A-bi-sai đáp: "Tôi sẽ đi với ông."
vi.R: Đa-vít nói với A-hi-mê-léc người Hê-tít và A-bi-sai, anh em với Giô-áp, mẹ là Xê-ru-gia. Ông hỏi họ: "Ai sẽ cùng tôi xuống trại của Sau-lơ?" A-bi-sai nói: "Tôi sẽ đi với ông."

decisions.choice: answered: spoke up
decisions.reason: "Answered" often means simply that someone began to speak in response to a situation, not to a question.

decisions.choice: Ahimelech the Hittite: a foreigner in David's band
decisions.reason: The Hittites were one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel (Genesis 23:3; Deuteronomy 7:1). Some served Israel's kings, as Uriah the Hittite later served David (2 Samuel 11:3). This Ahimelech is not the priest of chapters 21-22.

decisions.choice: Abishai son of Zeruiah: David's nephew
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), and her sons Joab, Abishai and Asahel are usually named after her. Abishai was to become one of David's leading warriors (2 Samuel 23:18).

decisions.choice: whose mother was Zeruiah
decisions.reason: Readable says who Zeruiah was, so that the reader does not take her for Abishai's father.

decisions.choice: Abishaï, fils de Tserouya, frère de Joab
decisions.reason: The forms the Samuel terms note sets; Readable says that Tserouya was his mother, as the English (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: Ahimelec el hitita; Abisai hijo de Sarvia
decisions.reason: Abishai and Zeruiah as the Samuel terms note has them (m3); Ahimelech the Hittite (m2) takes the same Spanish form as Ahimelech the priest, as the Hebrew name is the same.

decisions.choice: "A-hi-mê-léc người Hê-tít"; "A-bi-sai con trai Xê-ru-gia, anh em với Giô-áp"
decisions.reason: The terms note's names; Vietnamese must say whether a brother is older or younger, and the text does not, so "anh em với" leaves it open.

decisions.choice: Abishai says "ông" and "tôi" to David; David says "tôi"
decisions.reason: As for David's men elsewhere (23:3); Abishai is one of them.

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ דָוִ֨ד וַאֲבִישַׁ֥י׀אֶל־הָעָם֮ לַיְלָה֒ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שָׁא֗וּל שֹׁכֵ֤ב יָשֵׁן֙ בַּמַּעְגָּ֔ל וַחֲנִית֥וֹ מְעוּכָֽה־בָאָ֖רֶץ מְרַאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וְאַבְנֵ֣ר וְהָעָ֔ם שֹׁכְבִ֖ים סְבִיבֹתָֽיו׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came David and Abishai to the people by night, and look, Saul [was] lying asleep in the encampment, and his spear stuck in the ground at his head, and Abner and the people lying around him.

en.L: So David and Abishai came to the people by night, and look, Saul was lying asleep inside the encampment, with his spear stuck in the ground at his head, and Abner and the people were lying around him.
en.B: So David and Abishai went to the troops by night. There was Saul, lying asleep inside the ring of the camp, his spear thrust into the ground by his head, while Abner and the troops lay around him.
en.R: That night David and Abishai went down to the army. They found Saul asleep in the middle of the camp, with his spear stuck in the ground near his head. Abner and the soldiers were lying all around him.

es.L: Y llegaron David y Abisai al pueblo de noche, y he aquí que Saúl estaba acostado durmiendo dentro del cerco del campamento, con su lanza clavada en tierra a su cabecera, y Abner y el pueblo estaban acostados alrededor de él.
es.B: Así que David y Abisai fueron de noche hasta las tropas. Allí estaba Saúl, dormido dentro del cerco del campamento, con la lanza clavada en el suelo junto a su cabeza, mientras Abner y las tropas dormían a su alrededor.
es.R: Esa noche David y Abisai bajaron hasta el ejército. Encontraron a Saúl dormido en medio del campamento, con su lanza clavada en el suelo cerca de su cabeza. Abner y los soldados dormían a su alrededor.

fr.L: Et David et Abishaï vinrent de nuit vers le peuple, et voici, Saül était couché, endormi, à l’intérieur du campement, sa lance plantée en terre à son chevet, et Abner et le peuple étaient couchés autour de lui.
fr.B: David et Abishaï allèrent donc de nuit vers les troupes. Saül était là, couché et endormi au milieu du cercle du camp, sa lance plantée en terre près de sa tête, tandis qu’Abner et les troupes étaient couchés autour de lui.
fr.R: Cette nuit-là, David et Abishaï sont descendus vers l’armée. Ils ont trouvé Saül endormi au milieu du camp, sa lance plantée dans le sol près de sa tête. Abner et les soldats étaient couchés tout autour de lui.

vi.L: Vậy Đa-vít và A-bi-sai đến với quân lính ban đêm, và kìa, Sau-lơ đang nằm ngủ bên trong vòng trại, cây giáo cắm xuống đất ở đầu ông, còn Áp-ne và quân lính nằm chung quanh ông.
vi.B: Vậy ban đêm Đa-vít và A-bi-sai đi đến chỗ quân lính. Kìa, Sau-lơ đang nằm ngủ bên trong vòng trại, cây giáo cắm xuống đất cạnh đầu, còn Áp-ne và quân lính nằm chung quanh.
vi.R: Đêm đó Đa-vít và A-bi-sai đi xuống trại quân. Họ thấy Sau-lơ đang ngủ ở giữa trại, cây giáo cắm xuống đất gần đầu ông. Áp-ne và quân lính nằm chung quanh vua.

decisions.choice: look: the scene through David's eyes
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what David and Abishai find as they come into the camp.

decisions.choice: his spear stuck in the ground: the king's weapon
decisions.reason: Saul's spear marks his royal power and is never far from him (22:6). It is the spear he twice threw at David (18:10-11; 19:10). Stuck upright in the ground by his head, it also showed where the king slept.

decisions.choice: the troops; the army, the soldiers
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, for the people as an army in the field.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲבִישַׁי֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד סִגַּ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים הַיּ֛וֹם אֶת־אוֹיִבְךָ֖ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וְעַתָּה֩ אַכֶּ֨נּוּ נָ֜א בַּחֲנִ֤ית וּבָאָ֨רֶץ֙ פַּ֣עַם אַחַ֔ת וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁנֶ֖ה לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abishai to David, Has shut up God today your enemy into your hand; and now let me strike him, please, with the spear and into the ground [with] one stroke, and not will I do [it] twice to him.

en.L: And Abishai said to David, "God has delivered your enemy into your hand today. And now, please let me strike him with the spear, into the ground, with one stroke, and I will not [strike] him a second time."
en.B: Abishai said to David, "God has put your enemy in your power today. Now please let me drive the spear through him into the ground. One blow is all it will take; I will not need another."
en.R: Abishai said to David, "Today God has let you catch your enemy. Let me pin him to the ground with the spear. I will only need to hit him once."

es.L: Y dijo Abisai a David: «Dios ha entregado hoy a tu enemigo en tu mano. Ahora, pues, déjame, te ruego, clavarlo con la lanza en tierra de un solo golpe, y no le daré un segundo».
es.B: Abisai le dijo a David: «Hoy Dios ha puesto a tu enemigo en tu poder. Ahora, por favor, déjame atravesarlo con la lanza y clavarlo en el suelo. Con un solo golpe basta; no necesitaré otro».
es.R: Abisai le dijo a David: «Hoy Dios ha dejado que atrapes a tu enemigo. Déjame clavarlo en el suelo con la lanza. Solo tendré que darle una vez».

fr.L: Et Abishaï dit à David : « Dieu a livré aujourd’hui ton ennemi dans ta main. Et maintenant, laisse-moi, je te prie, le frapper de la lance jusque dans la terre, d’un seul coup, et je ne [le frapperai] pas une seconde fois. »
fr.B: Abishaï dit à David : « Aujourd’hui, Dieu a mis ton ennemi en ton pouvoir. Laisse-moi donc le clouer au sol avec la lance. Un seul coup suffira ; je n’aurai pas besoin d’y revenir. »
fr.R: Abishaï a dit à David : « Aujourd’hui, Dieu t’a permis d’attraper ton ennemi. Laisse-moi le clouer au sol avec sa lance. Je n’aurai besoin de frapper qu’une seule fois. »

vi.L: A-bi-sai nói với Đa-vít: "Hôm nay Đức Chúa Trời đã nộp kẻ thù của ông vào tay ông. Vậy bây giờ, xin để tôi dùng giáo đâm hắn ghim xuống đất chỉ một nhát thôi, tôi sẽ không cần đâm hắn lần thứ hai."
vi.B: A-bi-sai nói với Đa-vít: "Hôm nay Đức Chúa Trời đã phó kẻ thù vào tay ông. Bây giờ xin để tôi dùng giáo đâm thấu hắn xuống đất. Chỉ một nhát là đủ, không cần nhát thứ hai."
vi.R: A-bi-sai nói với Đa-vít: "Hôm nay Đức Chúa Trời đã cho ông bắt được kẻ thù. Xin để tôi dùng giáo ghim hắn xuống đất. Tôi chỉ cần đâm một lần thôi."

decisions.choice: delivered: shut up, handed over
decisions.reason: The verb means to close someone in so that they cannot escape, and so to hand them over (23:7, 20; 24:19).

decisions.choice: your enemy into your hand: as in the cave
decisions.reason: David's men said almost the same in the cave at En Gedi (24:5). Abishai reads the moment the same way: God has given Saul to David to kill.

decisions.choice: one stroke, and not twice: a single blow will do
decisions.reason: Abishai promises a quick, clean kill: one thrust of the spear will be enough.

decisions.choice: in your power; let you catch
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "into your hand"; Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־אֲבִישַׁ֖י אַל־תַּשְׁחִיתֵ֑הוּ כִּ֠י מִ֣י שָׁלַ֥ח יָד֛וֹ בִּמְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה וְנִקָּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Abishai, Do not destroy him, for who has stretched out his hand against [the] anointed of Yahweh and been guiltless?

en.L: And David said to Abishai, "Do not destroy him, for who has stretched out his hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed and been guiltless?"
en.B: But David said to Abishai, "Do not kill him. Who could raise his hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed and not be held guilty?"
en.R: But David told Abishai, "Do not kill him! No one can attack the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed and still be innocent."

es.L: Y dijo David a Abisai: «No lo destruyas, porque ¿quién extenderá su mano contra el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y quedará sin culpa?».
es.B: Pero David le dijo a Abisai: «No lo mates. ¿Quién podría levantar la mano contra el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y quedar sin culpa?».
es.R: Pero David le dijo a Abisai: «¡No lo mates! Nadie puede atacar al rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido y seguir siendo inocente».

fr.L: Et David dit à Abishaï : « Ne le détruis pas, car qui a étendu la main contre l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et est resté innocent ? »
fr.B: Mais David dit à Abishaï : « Ne le tue pas. Qui pourrait lever la main sur l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sans en être tenu pour coupable ? »
fr.R: Mais David a dit à Abishaï : « Ne le tue pas ! Personne ne peut attaquer le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint et rester innocent. »

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với A-bi-sai: "Đừng hủy diệt người, vì ai đã giơ tay hại người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà vô tội được?"
vi.B: Nhưng Đa-vít nói với A-bi-sai: "Đừng giết người. Ai có thể giơ tay hại vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu mà khỏi mắc tội?"
vi.R: Nhưng Đa-vít bảo A-bi-sai: "Đừng giết người! Không ai có thể tấn công vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu mà vẫn vô tội được."

decisions.choice: the anointed of Yahweh: the king Yahweh has set apart
decisions.reason: As at 24:7: Saul was set apart as king when Samuel poured oil on his head at Yahweh's command (10:1), so to kill him would be to strike at Yahweh, who chose him. David had already refused on these grounds in the cave (24:7, 11).

decisions.choice: stretch out his hand against: attack, harm
decisions.reason: To "send out the hand" against someone is to do them violence (22:17; 24:7, 11).

decisions.choice: been guiltless: gone unpunished
decisions.reason: The verb means to be clear of guilt and so free from punishment. The question expects the answer "no one".

decisions.choice: destroy: kill
decisions.reason: The verb, "bring to ruin", here means to take Saul's life.

decisions.choice: the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: As at 24:7, Readable spells out what "the LORD's anointed" means; Literal and Balanced keep the title.

decisions.choice: kill
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what Abishai means to do; Literal keeps "destroy".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ חַי־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אִם־יְהוָ֖ה יִגָּפֶ֑נּוּ אֽוֹ־יוֹמ֤וֹ יָבוֹא֙ וָמֵ֔ת א֧וֹ בַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה יֵרֵ֖ד וְנִסְפָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, [As] lives Yahweh, surely Yahweh will strike him, or his day will come and he will die, or into battle he will go down and be swept away.

en.L: And David said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, surely {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike him; or his day will come and he will die; or he will go down into battle and be swept away.
en.B: David went on, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who will strike him down. Either his time will come and he will die, or he will go out to battle and be cut down.
en.R: David said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will strike Saul down. Or Saul will die when his time comes, or he will be killed in battle.

es.L: Y dijo David: «Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo herirá; o llegará su día y morirá; o bajará a la batalla y perecerá.
es.B: David añadió: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive, es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien lo herirá. O le llegará su hora y morirá, o saldrá a la batalla y caerá en ella.
es.R: David dijo: «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mismo herirá a Saúl. O Saúl morirá cuando le llegue su hora, o lo matarán en la batalla.

fr.L: Et David dit : « [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui le frappera ; ou bien son jour viendra et il mourra ; ou bien il descendra à la bataille et il périra.
fr.B: David ajouta : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui le frappera. Ou bien son heure viendra et il mourra, ou bien il partira au combat et il y sera fauché.
fr.R: David a dit : « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} qui frappera Saül. Ou alors Saül mourra quand son heure viendra, ou bien il sera tué à la guerre.

vi.L: Đa-vít nói: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, chắc chắn {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đánh người; hoặc ngày của người sẽ đến và người sẽ chết; hoặc người sẽ ra trận và bị diệt.
vi.B: Đa-vít nói tiếp: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, chính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đánh phạt người. Hoặc đến ngày người sẽ chết, hoặc người sẽ ra trận và bị giết.
vi.R: Đa-vít nói: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, chính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ đánh phạt Sau-lơ. Hoặc Sau-lơ sẽ chết khi đến lúc, hoặc sẽ tử trận.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives: an oath
decisions.reason: Swearing by the life of Yahweh is the strongest oath (14:39; 20:3). David binds himself to leave Saul's death to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will strike him: judgment belongs to Yahweh
decisions.reason: David will not take Saul's life; if Saul is to die, Yahweh will see to it, as David told Saul in the cave (24:13, 16). Yahweh struck down Nabal in just this way (25:38).

decisions.choice: his day will come; be swept away
decisions.reason: "His day" is the day fixed for his death. The last verb means to be carried off or perish. Saul does in fact die in battle against the Philistines (31:1-6).

decisions.choice: be cut down; be killed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how a man is "swept away" in battle; Literal keeps the picture.

source.text: חָלִ֤ילָה לִּי֙ מֵֽיהוָ֔ה מִשְּׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בִּמְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠עַתָּה קַח־נָ֨א אֶֽת־הַחֲנִ֜ית אֲשֶׁ֧ר מְרַאֲשֹׁתָ֛יו וְאֶת־צַפַּ֥חַת הַמַּ֖יִם וְנֵ֥לֲכָה לָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Far be it to me from Yahweh from stretching out my hand against [the] anointed of Yahweh; and now take, please, the spear that [is] at his head and the jug of the water, and let us go for ourselves.

en.L: Far be it from me, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to stretch out my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed. But now, please take the spear that [is] at his head and the jug of water, and let us go."
en.B: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep me from ever raising my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed! Now pick up the spear beside his head and the water jug, and let us be on our way."
en.R: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} keep me from ever attacking the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed! Now grab the spear and the water jug near his head, and let us leave."

es.L: Lejos esté de mí, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, extender mi mano contra el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Pero ahora, toma, te ruego, la lanza que [está] a su cabecera y el jarro del agua, y vámonos».
es.B: ¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me libre de levantar jamás la mano contra el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! Ahora toma la lanza que está junto a su cabeza y el jarro de agua, y vámonos».
es.R: ¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me guarde de atacar jamás al rey que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha ungido! Ahora agarra la lanza y el jarro de agua que están cerca de su cabeza, y vámonos».

fr.L: Loin de moi, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, d’étendre la main contre l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! Mais maintenant, prends donc la lance qui [est] à son chevet et la cruche d’eau, et allons-nous-en. »
fr.B: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me garde de jamais lever la main sur l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! Prends plutôt la lance qui est près de sa tête et la cruche d’eau, et partons. »
fr.R: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’empêche d’attaquer un jour le roi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a oint ! Maintenant, prends la lance et la cruche d’eau qui sont près de sa tête, et partons. »

vi.L: Trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, tôi không bao giờ giơ tay hại người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Nhưng bây giờ, hãy lấy cây giáo ở đầu người và bình nước, rồi chúng ta đi."
vi.B: Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giữ tôi khỏi giơ tay hại vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu! Bây giờ anh hãy lấy cây giáo cạnh đầu người và bình nước, rồi chúng ta đi."
vi.R: Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giữ tôi khỏi tấn công vị vua {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã xức dầu! Bây giờ anh hãy lấy cây giáo và bình nước gần đầu người, rồi chúng ta đi."

decisions.choice: far be it from me from Yahweh: Yahweh forbid that I should
decisions.reason: A strong refusal, made in Yahweh's sight, with the same words David used in the cave (24:7).

decisions.choice: the jug of water: a traveler's water flask
decisions.reason: In the dry wilderness a man kept water close at hand through the night. The spear and the water jug from beside the king's head would prove that David had stood over him while he slept (verse 16), as the corner of his robe had done in the cave (24:5, 12).

decisions.choice: May the LORD keep me from
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the oath-like refusal into a wish addressed to the LORD; Literal keeps "far be it from me".

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶֽת־הַחֲנִ֜ית וְאֶת־צַפַּ֤חַת הַמַּ֨יִם֙ מֵרַאֲשֹׁתֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֣ין רֹאֶה֩ וְאֵ֨ין יוֹדֵ֜עַ וְאֵ֣ין מֵקִ֗יץ כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ יְשֵׁנִ֔ים כִּ֚י תַּרְדֵּמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה נָפְלָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took David the spear and the jug of the water from at [the] head of Saul, and they went for themselves; and [there was] none seeing and none knowing and none waking, for all of them [were] sleeping, for a deep sleep of Yahweh had fallen upon them.

en.L: So David took the spear and the jug of water from beside Saul's head, and they went away. And no one saw, and no one knew, and no one woke up, for all of them [were] asleep, because a deep sleep from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had fallen on them.
en.B: So David took the spear and the water jug from beside Saul's head, and the two of them left. No one saw them, no one knew, and no one woke up. They were all asleep, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had sent a deep sleep on them.
en.R: So David took the spear and the water jug that were near Saul's head, and he and Abishai left. Nobody saw them. Nobody knew what had happened. Nobody woke up. They were all sound asleep, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had made them sleep very deeply.

es.L: Y tomó David la lanza y el jarro del agua de la cabecera de Saúl, y se fueron. Y no hubo quien viera, ni quien supiera, ni quien despertara, porque todos ellos [estaban] dormidos, pues un sueño profundo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} había caído sobre ellos.
es.B: David tomó la lanza y el jarro de agua de junto a la cabeza de Saúl, y los dos se fueron. Nadie los vio, nadie se enteró y nadie se despertó. Todos estaban dormidos, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les había enviado un sueño profundo.
es.R: Así que David tomó la lanza y el jarro de agua que estaban cerca de la cabeza de Saúl, y él y Abisai se fueron. Nadie los vio. Nadie supo lo que había pasado. Nadie se despertó. Todos estaban profundamente dormidos, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los había hecho dormir muy profundamente.

fr.L: Et David prit la lance et la cruche d’eau du chevet de Saül, et ils s’en allèrent. Et personne ne vit, et personne ne sut, et personne ne s’éveilla, car tous dormaient, parce qu’un profond sommeil venant {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} était tombé sur eux.
fr.B: David prit donc la lance et la cruche d’eau qui étaient près de la tête de Saül, et ils s’en allèrent tous les deux. Personne ne les vit, personne ne s’en aperçut, personne ne se réveilla. Ils dormaient tous, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait fait tomber sur eux un profond sommeil.
fr.R: Alors David a pris la lance et la cruche d’eau qui étaient près de la tête de Saül, et Abishaï et lui sont partis. Personne ne les a vus. Personne n’a su ce qui s’était passé. Personne ne s’est réveillé. Ils dormaient tous profondément, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les avait plongés dans un sommeil très lourd.

vi.L: Đa-vít lấy cây giáo và bình nước ở đầu Sau-lơ, rồi họ đi. Không ai thấy, không ai biết, không ai thức dậy, vì tất cả đều ngủ, vì một giấc ngủ say từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên họ.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít lấy cây giáo và bình nước cạnh đầu Sau-lơ, rồi hai người ra đi. Không ai thấy, không ai biết, không ai thức dậy. Tất cả đều ngủ, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã cho một giấc ngủ say giáng trên họ.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít lấy cây giáo và bình nước gần đầu Sau-lơ, rồi ông và A-bi-sai ra đi. Không ai thấy họ. Không ai biết chuyện gì đã xảy ra. Không ai thức dậy. Tất cả đều ngủ say, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm cho họ ngủ rất say.

decisions.choice: a deep sleep of Yahweh: a sleep sent by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word names an unusually heavy sleep, one that Yahweh brings (Genesis 2:21; 15:12). The camp's failure to wake is Yahweh's doing, not only the guards' carelessness.

decisions.choice: David took: David himself takes them
decisions.reason: David had told Abishai to take the spear and jug (verse 11), but the narrator says that David took them. Either David carried them himself or the act is credited to him as leader; what matters is that they came from beside the king's head.

decisions.choice: none seeing, none knowing, none waking
decisions.reason: Three short clauses in a row stress how completely the camp slept.

decisions.choice: he and Abishai
decisions.reason: Readable names the two who left.

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר דָּוִד֙ הָעֵ֔בֶר וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד עַל־רֹאשׁ־הָהָ֖ר מֵֽרָחֹ֑ק רַ֥ב הַמָּק֖וֹם בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And crossed over David [to] the other side and stood on [the] top of the mountain from far; great [was] the space between them.

en.L: And David crossed over to the other side and stood on the top of the mountain far off; great [was] the space between them.
en.B: Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the hill some way off, with a wide space between them.
en.R: Then David crossed over to the other side of the valley. He stood on top of a hill a long way from the camp.

es.L: Y pasó David al otro lado y se puso en la cumbre del monte, a lo lejos; grande [era] el espacio entre ellos.
es.B: Luego David pasó al otro lado y se puso en la cumbre de la colina, a cierta distancia, con un gran espacio entre ellos.
es.R: Luego David cruzó al otro lado del valle. Se paró en la cima de una colina, muy lejos del campamento.

fr.L: Et David passa de l’autre côté et se tint au sommet de la montagne, au loin ; grand [était] l’espace entre eux.
fr.B: Puis David passa de l’autre côté et se tint au sommet de la colline, à bonne distance, avec un grand espace entre eux.
fr.R: Ensuite, David a traversé la vallée. Il s’est mis au sommet d’une colline, loin du camp.

vi.L: Đa-vít đi qua phía bên kia và đứng trên đỉnh núi từ xa; khoảng cách giữa họ [thì] lớn.
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít đi qua phía bên kia và đứng trên đỉnh đồi ở đằng xa, cách họ một khoảng rộng.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít đi qua phía bên kia thung lũng. Ông đứng trên đỉnh một ngọn đồi, cách xa trại quân.

decisions.choice: far off, with a great space between them
decisions.reason: David stands where his voice will carry across the valley but where no soldier can reach him quickly. In the cave he had spoken to Saul from close behind him (24:9).

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hilltop
decisions.reason: The word covers anything from a mountain to a hill or the hill country. Here it is a height across a valley from Saul's camp.

decisions.choice: hill
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "hill" for the height in this hill country; Literal keeps "mountain".

decisions.choice: of the valley
decisions.reason: Readable says what lay between David and the camp.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֨א דָוִ֜ד אֶל־הָעָ֗ם וְאֶל־אַבְנֵ֤ר בֶּן־נֵר֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא תַעֲנֶ֖ה אַבְנֵ֑ר וַיַּ֤עַן אַבְנֵר֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה קָרָ֥אתָ אֶל־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And called David to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, Will you not answer, Abner? And answered Abner and said, Who [are] you [that] you have called to the king?

en.L: And David called to the people and to Abner son of Ner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" And Abner answered and said, "Who [are] you [that] you have called to the king?"
en.B: David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, "Abner, are you not going to answer?" Abner replied, "Who are you, to call out to the king?"
en.R: David shouted to the soldiers and to Abner son of Ner, "Abner! Answer me!" Abner called back, "Who are you? Why are you shouting at the king?"

es.L: Y gritó David al pueblo y a Abner hijo de Ner, diciendo: «¿No responderás, Abner?». Y respondió Abner y dijo: «¿Quién [eres] tú, que gritas al rey?».
es.B: David les gritó a las tropas y a Abner hijo de Ner: «Abner, ¿no vas a responder?». Abner contestó: «¿Quién eres tú, que le gritas al rey?».
es.R: David les gritó a los soldados y a Abner hijo de Ner: «¡Abner! ¡Contéstame!». Abner le respondió a gritos: «¿Quién eres? ¿Por qué le gritas al rey?».

fr.L: Et David appela le peuple et Abner, fils de Ner, en disant : « Ne répondras-tu pas, Abner ? » Et Abner répondit et dit : « Qui [es]-tu, toi qui appelles le roi ? »
fr.B: David cria aux troupes et à Abner, fils de Ner : « Abner, tu ne réponds pas ? » Abner répondit : « Qui es-tu, toi qui cries ainsi vers le roi ? »
fr.R: David a crié aux soldats et à Abner, fils de Ner : « Abner ! Réponds-moi ! » Abner a crié à son tour : « Qui es-tu ? Pourquoi est-ce que tu cries vers le roi ? »

vi.L: Đa-vít gọi quân lính và Áp-ne con trai Nê-rơ: "Áp-ne, ông không trả lời sao?" Áp-ne trả lời: "Ngươi [là] ai mà kêu gọi vua?"
vi.B: Đa-vít lớn tiếng gọi quân lính và Áp-ne con trai Nê-rơ: "Áp-ne, ông không trả lời sao?" Áp-ne đáp: "Ngươi là ai mà dám kêu gọi vua?"
vi.R: Đa-vít hét lớn với quân lính và Áp-ne con trai Nê-rơ: "Áp-ne! Trả lời tôi đi!" Áp-ne đáp lại: "Ngươi là ai? Sao lại la hét với vua?"

decisions.choice: will you not answer: a summons
decisions.reason: The question is a call to wake up and respond.

decisions.choice: who are you that you have called to the king: a rebuke
decisions.reason: Abner asks who the caller is and also scolds him for shouting at the king's camp in the night. He does not yet know the voice.

decisions.choice: the troops; the soldiers
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, for the people as an army in the field.

decisions.choice: Who are you? Why are you shouting at the king?
decisions.reason: Readable splits Abner's question in two to bring out the rebuke in it.

decisions.choice: David says "ông" to Abner, mocking; Abner, not knowing him, says "ngươi"
decisions.reason: Abner speaks down to an unknown voice that disturbs the king (m2); David keeps a mocking courtesy.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶל־אַבְנֵ֜ר הֲלוֹא־אִ֣ישׁ אַתָּ֗ה וּמִ֤י כָמ֨וֹךָ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלָ֨מָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔רְתָּ אֶל־אֲדֹנֶ֖יךָ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּי־בָא֙ אַחַ֣ד הָעָ֔ם לְהַשְׁחִ֖ית אֶת־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David to Abner, [Are] not you a man? And who [is] like you in Israel? And why have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For came one of the people to destroy the king your lord.

en.L: And David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who [is] like you in Israel? Then why have you not kept watch over your lord the king? For one of the people came to destroy the king your lord.
en.B: David said to Abner, "You are a man, are you not? Who else in Israel is like you? Then why did you not guard your lord the king? One of the people came in to kill the king, your lord.
en.R: David said to Abner, "You are a brave man, are you not? There is no one in Israel like you! So why did you not guard your master, the king? Someone came into the camp to kill your master, the king!

es.L: Y dijo David a Abner: «¿No eres tú un hombre? ¿Y quién [hay] como tú en Israel? ¿Por qué, pues, no has vigilado a tu señor el rey? Porque vino uno del pueblo a destruir al rey tu señor.
es.B: David le dijo a Abner: «Tú eres un hombre, ¿no? ¿Quién hay en Israel como tú? Entonces, ¿por qué no protegiste a tu señor el rey? Uno de la tropa entró para matar al rey, tu señor.
es.R: David le dijo a Abner: «Tú eres un hombre valiente, ¿no? ¡No hay nadie en Israel como tú! Entonces, ¿por qué no cuidaste a tu señor, el rey? ¡Alguien entró en el campamento para matar a tu señor, el rey!

fr.L: Et David dit à Abner : « N’[es]-tu pas un homme ? Et qui [est] comme toi en Israël ? Et pourquoi n’as-tu pas veillé sur ton seigneur le roi ? Car quelqu’un du peuple est venu pour détruire le roi ton seigneur.
fr.B: David dit à Abner : « Tu es un homme, n’est-ce pas ? Qui donc en Israël est ton égal ? Alors pourquoi n’as-tu pas gardé ton seigneur le roi ? Quelqu’un du peuple est entré pour tuer le roi, ton seigneur.
fr.R: David a dit à Abner : « Tu es un homme courageux, non ? Personne en Israël n’est comme toi ! Alors pourquoi est-ce que tu n’as pas protégé ton maître, le roi ? Quelqu’un est entré dans le camp pour tuer ton maître, le roi !

vi.L: Đa-vít nói với Áp-ne: "Ông chẳng phải là đàn ông sao? Ai [bằng] ông trong Y-sơ-ra-ên? Vậy tại sao ông không canh giữ chúa ông là vua? Vì có một người trong dân đã đến để hủy diệt vua, chúa ông.
vi.B: Đa-vít nói với Áp-ne: "Ông là đàn ông, phải không? Trong Y-sơ-ra-ên ai bằng ông? Thế sao ông không bảo vệ chúa ông là vua? Có một người đã vào trại để giết vua, chúa của ông.
vi.R: Đa-vít nói với Áp-ne: "Ông là người dũng cảm, phải không? Trong Y-sơ-ra-ên không ai bằng ông! Thế sao ông không bảo vệ chủ ông là vua? Có người đã vào trại để giết vua, chủ của ông!

decisions.choice: are you not a man? who is like you? mockery
decisions.reason: David praises Abner as Israel's greatest soldier in order to shame him: the man with no equal has let his king lie unguarded.

decisions.choice: one of the people: someone
decisions.reason: "One of the people" means an ordinary man. David means himself or Abishai, though he does not yet say so.

decisions.choice: kept watch: guarded
decisions.reason: Abner's duty as commander was to watch over the king's person. David repeats the charge in verse 16.

decisions.choice: a brave man
decisions.reason: Readable adds "brave" to show that David is speaking of Abner's standing as a fighter.

decisions.choice: your master
decisions.reason: Readable says "master" for the lord a commander serves.

source.text: לֹא־ט֞וֹב הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּה֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂיתָ֒ חַי־יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י בְנֵי־מָ֨וֶת֙ אַתֶּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־שְׁמַרְתֶּ֛ם עַל־אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֖ם עַל־מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֣ה׀רְאֵ֗ה אֵֽי־חֲנִ֥ית הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְאֶת־צַפַּ֥חַת הַמַּ֖יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְרַאֲשֹׁתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Not good [is] the thing this that you have done. [As] lives Yahweh, surely sons of death [are] you, who have not kept watch over your lord, over [the] anointed of Yahweh. And now see where [is] the spear of the king and the jug of the water that [was] at his head.

en.L: This thing that you have done [is] not good. [As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you [are] sons of death, because you have not kept watch over your lord, over {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed. And now see where the king's spear [is], and the jug of water that [was] at his head."
en.B: You have not done well at all. As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you all deserve to die, because you did not guard your lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed. Now look around. Where is the king's spear, and the water jug that was by his head?"
en.R: You have not done your job well! As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, you and your men deserve to die. You did not protect your master, the king {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has anointed. Look around! Where is the king's spear? Where is the water jug that was near his head?"

es.L: No [es] buena esta cosa que has hecho. Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} hijos de muerte, porque no {{plural_you:han vigilado a su|habéis vigilado a vuestro}} señor, al ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Y ahora mira dónde [está] la lanza del rey y el jarro del agua que [estaba] a su cabecera».
es.B: Lo que has hecho no está nada bien. Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive, todos {{plural_you:ustedes merecen|vosotros merecéis}} la muerte, porque no {{plural_you:protegieron a su|protegisteis a vuestro}} señor, el ungido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Mira ahora a tu alrededor. ¿Dónde están la lanza del rey y el jarro de agua que estaban junto a su cabeza?».
es.R: ¡No has hecho bien tu trabajo! Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive, tú y tus hombres {{plural_you:merecen|merecéis}} morir. No {{plural_you:protegieron a su|protegisteis a vuestro}} señor, el rey que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha ungido. ¡Mira a tu alrededor! ¿Dónde está la lanza del rey? ¿Dónde está el jarro de agua que estaba cerca de su cabeza?».

fr.L: Ce que tu as fait là n’[est] pas bien. [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, vous [êtes] des fils de la mort, parce que vous n’avez pas veillé sur votre seigneur, sur l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Et maintenant, regarde où [est] la lance du roi, et la cruche d’eau qui [était] à son chevet. »
fr.B: Tu n’as pas bien agi. Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, vous méritez tous la mort, car vous n’avez pas gardé votre seigneur, l’oint {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Regarde donc : où est la lance du roi, et la cruche d’eau qui était près de sa tête ? »
fr.R: Tu n’as pas bien fait ton travail ! Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, tes hommes et toi, vous méritez de mourir. Vous n’avez pas protégé votre maître, le roi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a oint. Regarde autour de toi ! Où est la lance du roi ? Où est la cruche d’eau qui était près de sa tête ? »

vi.L: Việc ông đã làm không tốt. Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, các ông [là] con của sự chết, vì các ông đã không canh giữ chúa mình, là người được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Bây giờ hãy xem cây giáo của vua và bình nước ở đầu vua đâu rồi."
vi.B: Ông làm như vậy thật không tốt chút nào. Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, các ông đáng chết, vì đã không bảo vệ chúa mình, là vị vua được {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xức dầu. Bây giờ hãy nhìn xem, cây giáo của vua và bình nước cạnh đầu vua đâu rồi?"
vi.R: Ông đã không làm tròn bổn phận! Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, ông và quân lính của ông đáng chết. Các ông đã không bảo vệ chủ mình, là vị vua {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xức dầu. Hãy nhìn quanh xem! Cây giáo của vua đâu? Bình nước gần đầu vua đâu rồi?"

decisions.choice: sons of death: men who deserve to die
decisions.reason: "Son of death" means someone who has earned death (20:31; 2 Samuel 12:5). The word "you" is plural: Abner and the men who should have kept watch.

decisions.choice: over your lord, over the anointed of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The second phrase restates the first. The man they failed to guard was not only their master but Yahweh's anointed king.

decisions.choice: the spear and the water jug: the proof
decisions.reason: The missing objects show that someone stood by the sleeping king, as the cut corner of the robe did in 24:12.

decisions.choice: you and your men
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "you" here is plural.

decisions.choice: your master, the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: As in verses 9 and 15.

decisions.choice: vous (plural) for "sons of death"; tu for Abner
decisions.reason: "You" is plural in the Hebrew (m1): Abner and his men. French "vous" shows the shift that English "you" hides; Readable adds "tes hommes et toi", as the English (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: plural_you for “you are sons of death”
decisions.reason: David speaks to Abner, but the Hebrew turns to the plural for “you are sons of death” and “you have not kept watch”: Abner and the guard with him (m1; the English Readable says “you and your men”). The singular returns with “see”.

source.text: וַיַּכֵּ֤ר שָׁאוּל֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל דָּוִ֔ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֲקוֹלְךָ֥ זֶ֖ה בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד קוֹלִ֖י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And recognized Saul [the] voice of David and said, [Is] this your voice, my son David? And said David, My voice, my lord the king.

en.L: And Saul recognized David's voice and said, "[Is] this your voice, my son David?" And David said, "[It is] my voice, my lord the king."
en.B: Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David replied, "It is, my lord the king."
en.R: Saul knew it was David's voice. He called out, "Is that you, David my son?" David answered, "Yes, it is, my lord the king."

es.L: Y reconoció Saúl la voz de David, y dijo: «¿[Es] esta tu voz, hijo mío David?». Y dijo David: «Mi voz [es], mi señor el rey».
es.B: Saúl reconoció la voz de David y dijo: «¿Es esa tu voz, David, hijo mío?». David respondió: «Sí, lo es, mi señor el rey».
es.R: Saúl supo que era la voz de David. Le gritó: «¿Eres tú, David, hijo mío?». David le contestó: «Sí, soy yo, mi señor el rey».

fr.L: Et Saül reconnut la voix de David et dit : « [Est-]ce là ta voix, mon fils David ? » Et David dit : « [C’est] ma voix, mon seigneur le roi. »
fr.B: Saül reconnut la voix de David et dit : « Est-ce bien ta voix, mon fils David ? » David répondit : « Oui, mon seigneur le roi. »
fr.R: Saül a reconnu la voix de David. Il a crié : « C’est toi, David, mon fils ? » David a répondu : « Oui, c’est moi, mon seigneur le roi. »

vi.L: Sau-lơ nhận ra tiếng Đa-vít và nói: "Có phải tiếng của con đó không, Đa-vít con ta?" Đa-vít nói: "Thưa chúa tôi là vua, [đó là] tiếng tôi."
vi.B: Sau-lơ nhận ra tiếng Đa-vít và nói: "Có phải tiếng con đó không, Đa-vít con ta?" Đa-vít đáp: "Tâu bệ hạ, đúng là tiếng tôi."
vi.R: Sau-lơ biết đó là tiếng của Đa-vít. Vua gọi lớn: "Có phải con đó không, Đa-vít con ta?" Đa-vít đáp: "Tâu đức vua, đúng là tôi."

decisions.choice: is this your voice, my son David?
decisions.reason: Saul asks the same question as at En Gedi (24:17). Calling David "my son" is tender, and David was in fact his son-in-law (18:27).

decisions.choice: my lord the king: a subject's address
decisions.reason: David speaks to Saul with full respect as his king, even while Saul hunts him.

decisions.choice: Is that you
decisions.reason: Readable says what Saul means by "your voice"; Literal and Balanced keep the wording.

decisions.choice: Saul again says "con" and "ta" to David (26:17-25); David answers as a subject, "chúa tôi là vua" / "bệ hạ" / "đức vua" and "đầy tớ của vua" / "tôi"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: Saul says "con" where he says "my son"; here David does not say "my father", so he keeps the subject's words.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֛ה אֲדֹנִ֥י רֹדֵ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ כִּ֚י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּמַה־בְּיָדִ֖י רָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Why this [is] my lord pursuing after his servant? For what have I done, and what [is] in my hand [of] evil?

en.L: And he said, "Why [is] this my lord pursuing after his servant? For what have I done, and what evil [is] in my hand?
en.B: He went on, "Why is my lord chasing after his servant? What have I done? What wrong have I committed?
en.R: Then he said, "My lord, why are you chasing me, your servant? What have I done? What crime have I committed?

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Por qué persigue así mi señor a su siervo? Porque ¿qué he hecho, y qué mal [hay] en mi mano?
es.B: Y añadió: «¿Por qué persigue mi señor a su siervo? ¿Qué he hecho? ¿Qué mal he cometido?
es.R: Luego dijo: «Mi señor, ¿por qué me persigues a mí, tu siervo? ¿Qué he hecho? ¿Qué delito he cometido?

fr.L: Et il dit : « Pourquoi donc mon seigneur poursuit-il son serviteur ? Car qu’ai-je fait, et quel mal [y a-t-il] dans ma main ?
fr.B: Il ajouta : « Pourquoi mon seigneur poursuit-il son serviteur ? Qu’ai-je fait ? Quel mal ai-je commis ?
fr.R: Puis il a dit : « Mon seigneur, pourquoi est-ce que tu me poursuis, moi, ton serviteur ? Qu’est-ce que j’ai fait ? Quel crime ai-je commis ?

vi.L: Ông nói: "Tại sao chúa tôi đuổi theo đầy tớ của người? Tôi đã làm gì, và tay tôi có điều ác gì?
vi.B: Ông nói tiếp: "Tại sao bệ hạ lại đuổi theo đầy tớ của bệ hạ? Tôi đã làm gì? Tôi đã phạm điều sai trái gì?
vi.R: Rồi ông nói: "Tâu đức vua, sao vua lại đuổi theo tôi, là đầy tớ của vua? Tôi đã làm gì? Tôi đã phạm tội gì?

decisions.choice: his servant: David speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" or "his servant" was a polite way to address someone of higher rank (Genesis 18:3; 1 Samuel 20:7-8). David puts himself below Saul as his subject.

decisions.choice: what evil is in my hand: what wrong have I done
decisions.reason: The hand stands for what a person does. David had made the same claim in the cave (24:12) and to Jonathan (20:1).

decisions.choice: pursuing: hunting down
decisions.reason: The verb is used of chasing an enemy. David repeats the picture of the hunt in verse 20.

decisions.choice: My lord, why are you chasing me, your servant?
decisions.reason: Readable turns David's third-person way of speaking into direct address, keeping "your servant".

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה יִֽשְׁמַֽע־נָא֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י עַבְדּ֑וֹ אִם־יְהוָ֞ה הֱסִֽיתְךָ֥ בִי֙ יָרַ֣ח מִנְחָ֔ה וְאִ֣ם׀בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֗ם אֲרוּרִ֥ים הֵם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־גֵרְשׁ֣וּנִי הַיּ֗וֹם מֵהִסְתַּפֵּ֜חַ בְּנַחֲלַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֵ֥ךְ עֲבֹ֖ד אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And now let hear, please, my lord the king [the] words of his servant: If Yahweh has stirred you up against me, let him smell an offering; but if [the] sons of man, cursed [are] they before Yahweh, for they have driven me out today from attaching myself to [the] inheritance of Yahweh, saying, Go, serve other gods.

en.L: And now, please let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has stirred you up against me, let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} smell an offering; but if [it is] the sons of man, cursed [are] they before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for they have driven me out today from having a share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s inheritance, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'
en.B: Now please, my lord the king, listen to the words of your servant. If it is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who has stirred you up against me, may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accept an offering. But if it is human beings, may they be cursed before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! For they have driven me out today from my share in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s inheritance, as if to say, 'Go, serve other gods.'
en.R: My lord the king, please listen to what your servant has to say. If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has turned you against me, may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} accept an offering and be pleased. But if people have turned you against me, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} curse them! Today they have chased me out of the land that belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is as if they were telling me, 'Go away and worship other gods.'

es.L: Ahora, pues, escuche, te ruego, mi señor el rey las palabras de su siervo. Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha incitado contra mí, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} acepte el olor de una ofrenda; pero si [son] los hijos de los hombres, malditos [sean] ellos delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque me han echado hoy para que no tenga parte en la heredad {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, diciendo: “Ve, sirve a otros dioses”.
es.B: Ahora, por favor, mi señor el rey, escucha las palabras de tu siervo. Si es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien te ha incitado contra mí, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} acepte una ofrenda. Pero si son los hombres, ¡que sean malditos delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! Porque hoy me han echado de mi parte en la heredad {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, como si dijeran: “Vete a servir a otros dioses”.
es.R: Mi señor el rey, por favor, escucha lo que tu siervo tiene que decirte. Si es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien te ha puesto en contra mía, que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} acepte una ofrenda y quede satisfecho. Pero si es la gente la que te ha puesto en contra mía, ¡que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los maldiga! Hoy me han echado de la tierra que le pertenece {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Es como si me dijeran: “Vete de aquí y adora a otros dioses”.

fr.L: Et maintenant, que mon seigneur le roi écoute donc les paroles de son serviteur : si c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui t’a excité contre moi, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} respire [le parfum d’]une offrande ; mais si [ce sont] les fils des hommes, qu’ils soient maudits devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car ils m’ont chassé aujourd’hui pour que je n’aie pas de part à l’héritage {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, en disant : “Va, sers d’autres dieux !”
fr.B: Maintenant, je t’en prie, mon seigneur le roi, écoute les paroles de ton serviteur. Si c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui t’a poussé contre moi, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} agrée une offrande. Mais si ce sont des êtres humains, qu’ils soient maudits devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Car ils m’ont chassé aujourd’hui de ma part dans l’héritage {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, comme pour me dire : “Va servir d’autres dieux !”
fr.R: Mon seigneur le roi, écoute, s’il te plaît, ce que ton serviteur a à te dire. Si c’est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui t’a dressé contre moi, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} accepte une offrande et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit satisfait. Mais si ce sont des gens qui t’ont dressé contre moi, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les maudisse ! Aujourd’hui, ils m’ont chassé du pays qui appartient {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. C’est comme s’ils me disaient : “Va-t’en adorer d’autres dieux !”

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, xin chúa tôi là vua nghe lời của đầy tớ người: Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xui giục vua chống lại tôi, thì nguyện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngửi một của lễ; nhưng nếu là con cái loài người, thì nguyện họ bị nguyền rủa trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì ngày nay họ đã đuổi tôi đi, không cho tôi gắn bó với cơ nghiệp của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, mà nói rằng: 'Hãy đi, phục vụ các thần khác.'
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, tâu bệ hạ, xin bệ hạ nghe lời đầy tớ của bệ hạ. Nếu chính {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã xui giục bệ hạ chống lại tôi, nguyện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhậm một của lễ. Nhưng nếu là loài người, nguyện họ bị nguyền rủa trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}! Vì hôm nay họ đã đuổi tôi ra khỏi phần cơ nghiệp của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, như thể bảo tôi: 'Hãy đi phục vụ các thần khác.'
vi.R: Tâu đức vua, xin vua nghe tôi nói. Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã khiến vua chống lại tôi, xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhận một của lễ và hài lòng. Nhưng nếu người ta đã khiến vua chống lại tôi, xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nguyền rủa họ! Hôm nay họ đã đuổi tôi ra khỏi xứ thuộc về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Như thể họ bảo tôi: 'Hãy đi nơi khác mà thờ các thần khác.'

decisions.choice: let him smell an offering: may Yahweh accept a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Yahweh is said to "smell" the soothing smell of a sacrifice when he accepts it and his anger is turned away (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 26:31). If Yahweh is behind Saul's hatred, David asks that an offering be made to set things right with him.

decisions.choice: the sons of man: human beings
decisions.reason: The phrase sets people against Yahweh: if Saul's anger comes from slanderers and not from Yahweh, they are the guilty ones (24:10).

decisions.choice: driven me out from attaching myself to the inheritance of Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to join oneself to or have a part in something. "The inheritance of Yahweh" is the land and people of Israel, which belong to Yahweh as his own possession (Deuteronomy 32:9; 2 Samuel 14:16; 20:19). Hunted out of Israel, David loses his place among Yahweh's people.

decisions.choice: go, serve other gods: exile from Yahweh's land
decisions.reason: In the ancient world each land was thought to belong to its own god, and Yahweh's worship was bound to his land, his people and his sanctuary (Deuteronomy 4:27-28; 28:36, 64; 2 Kings 5:17; Ruth 1:15-16). To drive David out of Israel was, in effect, to send him where other gods were worshiped and cut him off from the worship of Yahweh. David does not say that he will serve other gods; he says that his enemies are as good as telling him to. He goes to the Philistines in the next chapter (27:1).

decisions.choice: saying: as if to say
decisions.reason: No one has actually spoken the words. "Saying" gives the meaning of what David's enemies are doing to him.

decisions.choice: as if to say; It is as if they were telling me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "saying" gives the effect of their actions, not words anyone spoke.

decisions.choice: the land that belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what Yahweh's inheritance is here; Literal and Balanced keep "inheritance".

decisions.choice: que él acepte el olor de una ofrenda (L); que él acepte una ofrenda (B, R)
decisions.reason: “Let him smell an offering” means may the LORD accept a sacrifice (m1). Literal keeps the smell with “el olor”; Balanced and Readable say “acepte”, as the English does.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה אַל־יִפֹּ֤ל דָּֽמִי֙ אַ֔רְצָה מִנֶּ֖גֶד פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּֽי־יָצָ֞א מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֣שׁ אֶחָ֔ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יִרְדֹּ֥ף הַקֹּרֵ֖א בֶּהָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And now let not fall my blood to the ground away from [the] presence of Yahweh, for has come out [the] king of Israel to seek a flea, one, as hunts the partridge in the mountains.

en.L: And now, do not let my blood fall to the ground away from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for the king of Israel has come out to seek a single flea, as one hunts the partridge in the mountains."
en.B: So now, do not let my blood be spilled on the ground far from the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The king of Israel has come out to hunt for a single flea, the way someone chases a partridge through the hills."
en.R: Do not let me be killed far away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s presence. The king of Israel has come out to look for one tiny flea! He is hunting me like someone hunting a partridge in the hills."

es.L: Ahora, pues, no caiga mi sangre en tierra lejos de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, porque el rey de Israel ha salido a buscar una sola pulga, como quien persigue la perdiz por los montes».
es.B: Así que no dejes que mi sangre se derrame en tierra lejos de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. El rey de Israel ha salido a cazar una sola pulga, como quien persigue una perdiz por los montes».
es.R: No dejes que me maten lejos de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. ¡El rey de Israel ha salido a buscar una pulguita! Me está cazando como quien caza una perdiz en los montes».

fr.L: Et maintenant, que mon sang ne tombe pas à terre loin de la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, car le roi d’Israël est sorti pour chercher une seule puce, comme on chasse la perdrix dans les montagnes. »
fr.B: Maintenant donc, ne laisse pas mon sang couler sur la terre, loin de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Le roi d’Israël est sorti à la recherche d’une simple puce, comme on poursuit une perdrix dans les montagnes. »
fr.R: Ne me fais pas mourir loin de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Le roi d’Israël est sorti pour chercher une toute petite puce ! Il me chasse comme on chasse une perdrix dans les collines. »

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, xin đừng để máu tôi đổ xuống đất xa cách sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, vì vua Y-sơ-ra-ên đã ra đi tìm một con bọ chét, như người ta săn chim đa đa trên núi."
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, xin đừng để máu tôi đổ xuống đất xa cách sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Vua Y-sơ-ra-ên đã ra đi săn lùng một con bọ chét, như người ta đuổi bắt chim đa đa trên đồi núi."
vi.R: Xin đừng để tôi bị giết ở nơi xa cách sự hiện diện của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Vua Y-sơ-ra-ên đã ra đi để tìm một con bọ chét nhỏ bé! Vua săn đuổi tôi như người ta săn chim đa đa trên đồi."

decisions.choice: let not my blood fall to the ground: do not let me be killed
decisions.reason: Blood falling to the ground is a picture of violent death (2 Samuel 14:11; 1 Kings 1:52).

decisions.choice: away from the presence of Yahweh: in a foreign land
decisions.reason: David picks up verse 19: if he is driven from Israel, he will die far from the land where Yahweh is worshiped.

decisions.choice: a single flea
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "a single flea", the same picture David used in 24:15 of how little he matters. An ancient Greek translation reads "to seek my life" here. The Hebrew reading fits the hunting picture that follows.

decisions.choice: the partridge: a hunted bird of the hills
decisions.reason: The bird is named "the caller", probably a partridge, which runs along the ground and is chased until it tires. The name echoes David "calling" from the hilltop (verse 14). The bird cannot be identified for certain.

decisions.choice: be killed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of "my blood fall to the ground"; Literal and Balanced keep the picture.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שָׁא֨וּל חָטָ֜אתִי שׁ֣וּב בְּנִֽי־דָוִ֗ד כִּ֠י לֹֽא־אָרַ֤ע לְךָ֙ ע֔וֹד תַּ֠חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָקְרָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֛י בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה הִנֵּ֥ה הִסְכַּ֛לְתִּי וָאֶשְׁגֶּ֖ה הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Saul, I have sinned. Return, my son David, for not will I harm you again, because was precious my life in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have erred very greatly.

en.L: And Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will not harm you again, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Look, I have acted foolishly and have gone very greatly astray."
en.B: Then Saul said, "I have sinned. My son David, come back. Since you held my life precious today, I will not do you harm again. I have been a fool, and I have done a very great wrong."
en.R: Saul said, "I have done wrong. Come back, David my son. You thought my life was worth saving today, so I will never try to hurt you again. I have been very foolish. I have made a terrible mistake."

es.L: Y dijo Saúl: «He pecado. Vuelve, hijo mío David, porque no te haré más mal, ya que mi vida fue preciosa a tus ojos este día. He aquí que he obrado neciamente y he errado en gran manera».
es.B: Entonces Saúl dijo: «He pecado. David, hijo mío, vuelve. Ya que hoy tuviste en tanto mi vida, no volveré a hacerte daño. He sido un necio, y he cometido un error muy grave».
es.R: Saúl dijo: «He hecho mal. Vuelve, David, hijo mío. Hoy pensaste que valía la pena salvar mi vida, así que nunca más trataré de hacerte daño. He sido muy necio. He cometido un error terrible».

fr.L: Et Saül dit : « J’ai péché. Reviens, mon fils David, car je ne te ferai plus de mal, parce que ma vie a été précieuse à tes yeux en ce jour. Voici, j’ai agi en insensé, et je me suis gravement égaré. »
fr.B: Alors Saül dit : « J’ai péché. Reviens, David, mon fils. Puisque ma vie a été précieuse à tes yeux aujourd’hui, je ne te ferai plus de mal. J’ai agi comme un insensé, et j’ai commis une très lourde faute. »
fr.R: Saül a dit : « J’ai mal agi. Reviens, David, mon fils. Aujourd’hui, tu as trouvé que ma vie valait la peine d’être épargnée. Alors je n’essaierai plus jamais de te faire du mal. J’ai été vraiment stupide. J’ai fait une terrible erreur. »

vi.L: Sau-lơ nói: "Ta đã phạm tội. Hãy trở về, Đa-vít con ta, vì ta sẽ không làm hại con nữa, bởi hôm nay mạng sống ta đã quý giá trước mắt con. Kìa, ta đã hành động dại dột và đã lầm lạc quá lắm."
vi.B: Bấy giờ Sau-lơ nói: "Ta đã phạm tội. Đa-vít con ta, hãy trở về. Vì hôm nay con đã quý trọng mạng sống ta, ta sẽ không làm hại con nữa. Ta đã hành động như kẻ dại, và đã sai lầm rất nặng."
vi.R: Sau-lơ nói: "Ta đã làm điều sai trái. Hãy trở về, Đa-vít con ta. Hôm nay con đã coi mạng sống ta là đáng cứu, nên ta sẽ không bao giờ tìm cách hại con nữa. Ta thật dại dột. Ta đã phạm một lỗi lầm rất lớn."

decisions.choice: I have sinned: Saul's confession
decisions.reason: Saul admits his wrong, as he did to Samuel (15:24, 30) and wept over it at En Gedi (24:17-18). Yet David does not come back to him, and soon flees to the Philistines (27:1).

decisions.choice: my life was precious in your eyes: you valued my life
decisions.reason: David held Saul's life too dear to take it. David answers with the same picture in verse 24.

decisions.choice: acted foolishly and erred very greatly
decisions.reason: "Act foolishly" is the verb Samuel used of Saul in 13:13. The second verb means to go astray or blunder, and the words that follow make it very great.

decisions.choice: I have done wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says "done wrong" for the confession; Literal and Balanced keep "sinned".

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַן דָּוִד֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הִנֵּ֖ה חֲנִ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְיַעֲבֹ֛ר אֶחָ֥ד מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֖ים וְיִקָּחֶֽהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered David and said, Look, the spear of the king! And let cross over one of the young men and take it.

en.L: And David answered and said, "Look, the king's spear! Let one of the young men come over and take it.
en.B: David answered, "Here is the king's spear. Let one of your young men come across and get it.
en.R: David answered, "Here is the king's spear. Send one of your young men over to get it.

es.L: Y respondió David y dijo: «He aquí la lanza del rey. Que pase uno de los jóvenes y la tome.
es.B: David respondió: «Aquí está la lanza del rey. Que venga uno de tus jóvenes a buscarla.
es.R: David le contestó: «Aquí está la lanza del rey. Manda a uno de tus jóvenes a buscarla.

fr.L: Et David répondit et dit : « Voici la lance du roi ! Qu’un des jeunes gens passe [ici] et la prenne.
fr.B: David répondit : « Voici la lance du roi. Qu’un de tes jeunes gens traverse pour venir la prendre.
fr.R: David a répondu : « Voici la lance du roi. Envoie un de tes jeunes gens la chercher.

vi.L: Đa-vít trả lời: "Kìa, cây giáo của vua! Xin cho một trong các thanh niên qua đây lấy nó.
vi.B: Đa-vít đáp: "Đây là cây giáo của bệ hạ. Xin bệ hạ cho một thanh niên của bệ hạ sang lấy về.
vi.R: Đa-vít đáp: "Đây là cây giáo của đức vua. Xin vua sai một thanh niên của vua sang đây lấy.

decisions.choice: the king's spear
alternatives: Here is the spear, O king!
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text could be read "Here is the spear, O king!", while the reading noted in the margin is "Here is the king's spear". The text follows the margin. The meaning is the same: David hands back the king's spear.

decisions.choice: the young men: Saul's soldiers
decisions.reason: "Young men" here are fighting men or attendants of the king (14:1; 21:3).

decisions.choice: your young men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "your" to show that the young men are Saul's.

source.text: וַֽיהוָה֙ יָשִׁ֣יב לָאִ֔ישׁ אֶת־צִדְקָת֖וֹ וְאֶת־אֱמֻנָת֑וֹ אֲשֶׁר֩ נְתָנְךָ֨יְהוָ֤ה׀הַיּוֹם֙ בְּיָ֔ד וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֔יתִי לִשְׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בִּמְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh will repay to each his righteousness and his faithfulness, for gave you Yahweh today into [my] hand, and not was I willing to stretch out my hand against [the] anointed of Yahweh.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will repay each man [for] his righteousness and his faithfulness; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave you into [my] hand today, but I was not willing to stretch out my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} repays each person for his righteousness and his faithfulness. Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} put you in my power, but I would not raise my hand against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointed.
